A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling-law study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1's canonical sweep to v2's standardized sweep.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformer-training outcomes and fitted scaling laws for two CELLxGENE regimes, including seed-level loss ranges and entropy-floor estimates in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original standardized parameter sweep and reports held-out test results, a data-size sweep, residual diagnostics, and direct-NLL calibration outcomes.

M1.justification: The encoder, embeddings, mask token, prediction head, 15% masking, MSE objective, and scaling-fit procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B explicitly says the direct-NLL reruns differ only in additional validation logging. Revised parameter counts do not document a new architectural component.

E1.justification: V2 removes the 1,024-gene, 10,000-cell reconstruction setting, one of v1's two principal regimes, including its appendix coverage. It retains the 512-gene CELLxGENE task. The added 25k–200k subsets use the same gene set and preprocessing, so their sample-count variation belongs to E3.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally compares against external methods. scVI, scGPT, Geneformer, scBERT, and scFoundation remain related-work references, while the experiments compare sizes of the same transformer family.

E3.justification: V2 centers evaluation on the existing 18-run, 60k-step standardized sweep and removes the heterogeneous additional runs and XL setting. It adds reported held-out test evaluation, an M-model data-size sweep at fixed vocabulary and training steps, and XXS/TINY direct-NLL reruns. The original 90/5/5 split and canonical optimization settings remain.

E4.justification: New Section 7.3 and Figure 2 investigate data-size sensitivity and test the homoscedasticity assumption through per-gene held-out residuals. Section 7.5.3 and Appendix A add direct-versus-derived NLL calibration for XXS/TINY. V1 discussed these limitations without these empirical checks.

E5.justification: Table 2 changes from minimum–maximum seed ranges to means and standard deviations for validation and test MSE. The retained sweep still uses seeds 7, 8, and 9; this does not establish an increase in repetitions. No confidence intervals for scaling parameters or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: V2 removes Regime B results and the 21-run Regime A fit, replaces loss ranges with standardized means, and adds test results, including alpha=0.268, c=1.462, and R²=0.859. New findings include the nearly flat data-size fit, residual heterogeneity, and NLL calibration. The canonical validation fit and Table 4 entropy estimates remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same mathematical content, including the scaling formulation and Gaussian entropy conversion. Homoscedasticity was already assumed in v1 Appendix A. V2 adds empirical checks and interpretive qualifications, without new proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion withdraw v1's central claim that data scarcity is established as the binding constraint and that the data-to-parameter ratio determines scaling. V2 instead claims parameter scaling within one standardized setting, emphasizes test consistency and diagnostics, and explicitly limits the entropy estimate to task-specific remaining uncertainty.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the data-bottleneck and threshold interpretation with an interaction among data volume, effective epochs, and optimization budget. It corrects v1 Section 7.4.3's description of 2.3 bits as predictable information to remaining uncertainty. Residual heterogeneity now qualifies the Gaussian interpretation, and the new Broader Impact section discusses composition biases affecting the fitted floor.

D1.justification: V2 adds a dataset filename, configuration details for the supplementary experiments, the runs-directory location, and a manifest-filtering disclosure. Table 1 revises reported parameter counts, including TINY from 9,937 to 9,953 and L from 101,033,041 to 100,510,801. The repository and seed information remain; relocating reproducibility information to Appendix C is not a new code release.

R1.justification: The same 24 cited works and first-systematic-study positioning remain. However, v2 Section 7.4 drops v1's specific claim that its dual-regime behavior echoes Kaplan's parameter/data-scaling contradiction, replacing it with a qualified discussion of different scaling axes and insufficient evidence for an intersection analysis.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, regime descriptions, results narrative, discussion, limitations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the standardized sweep. The dual-regime organization is removed, Broader Impact is added, and reproducibility moves to Appendix C. Citation formatting also changes from author–year to numbered references.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 1 are substantially redesigned around standardized validation/test comparisons. A new Figure 2 displays the data-size sweep and residual scatter; v1 Figure 2 is retained as Figure 3 with a revised caption. Typography, headings, title presentation, and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves inferential reliability by withdrawing the unsupported causal conclusion from confounded regimes, correcting the entropy interpretation, and adding test confirmation and targeted diagnostics. These address central weaknesses while preserving the canonical scaling evidence. Coverage is narrower and entropy remains approximate. An unresolved discrepancy—Figure 2's 200k-cell M-model loss near 1.57 versus Table 2's 1.462 under apparently matching settings—limits the auxiliary sweep, but does not outweigh the stronger validation and more defensible conclusions.
